universal: Calls people by their trade instead of their name.

Likes proverbs and works one in when it fits.
Uses long words where short ones would do.

Gives people nicknames soon after meeting them.
Says no offense before saying something rude.
Starts most sentences with the word well.
Says if you ask me before opinions nobody asked for.

Corrects their own words in mid-sentence.

Uses soft words for death and violence.

Ends sentences with a tag question, such as right or yes.
Trails off at the end of sentences.
Describes people by what they carry.
Doubles words for emphasis, as in far, far away.
States every opinion as a known fact.
Uses hunting terms for everyday things.

Swears mildly in most sentences.
Never swears, and uses odd substitutes instead.

human: Gets attention with hoy or oi.
Drops the g from words that end in ing, as in lookin' and fightin'.
Says ain't for is not and am not.
Calls strangers outlander or drifter.

Calls hivers twig men.
Brings most topics back to food and the next meal.
Mentions a bad back or sore feet in passing.
Suggests a drink to mark any good news.

Talks about themselves in the third person when excited.
